tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a message to a teammate (by name) or to 'board' (team pins). Set reply_to to the #N of the message you answer. Another team or a solo session is reached only gate to gate: from your team's gate, send to the team's name (it reaches that team's gate) or the solo's name; see {tool:who}.

body.description: message text (empty only for board op=remove)

reply_to.description: #N of the message you are answering

kind.description: free-form label, not interpreted by piggery

op.description: assign: this mail is the current task of the member it goes to (it must report to you; shown in top; a later assign replaces it; give it a short title on the first line). replace | remove: board only

target.description: board only: #N of the pin to replace or remove

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: Read your unacknowledged piggery messages. view=board instead shows the team's pins (read-only, marks nothing as read).

tools.name: who
tools.description: List your team in full (state: idle, working, awaiting_permission, gone), then one line per other team and per solo session on this machine. Teams and solo sessions talk gate to gate only (replies too): write to a team's name to reach its gate; a solo session is its own gate. If you are not your team's gate, ask your gate to relay.

tools.name: agent
tools.description: Manage worker agents. spawn: start a worker (role, name, task; the task arrives as a message, and the worker's reply comes back to you as mail). spawn with template instead of role calls up a taskforce: a temporary team from a template that has a taskforce block (templates marks them), for a one-off job such as a second opinion or a review; the task goes to its chair, name is its team name (default: the template's), it works in your directory (or in cwd), reports to you and stays for follow-ups until you close it, and you stay where you are, unlike found. A solo session or a team's gate may call one on its own judgment; a taskforce never calls another. stop | resume | tail: target = worker name. admit: add a solo session marked admittable in {tool:who} (target) to a role you may spawn (role). templates: list the team templates found can use (summary and roles); read it to pick one. found: create a piggery team from a template (default p2p) rooted at the current directory and become its gate; if you are in a team you leave it. close: close your team (you must be its gate); you become solo and its workers stop. close with team = a taskforce you called ends it: only its caller closes it, a taskforce never closes itself. reopen: open again a closed team rooted at the current directory (team = its name) and become its gate; its stopped workers and unread mail come to you. admit, found, reopen and close of your own team only when the user asks. A solo session can only use templates, spawn with template, found, reopen and close of a taskforce it called.

action.description: spawn | stop | resume | tail | admit | templates | found | close | reopen

template.description: found: team template name (default p2p). spawn: a taskforce template instead of role (never both)

team.description: reopen: the closed team's name. close: a taskforce you called (none: your own team)

role.description: spawn/admit: the role (spawn: instead of template, never both)

name.description: spawn: the worker's name; with template, the taskforce's team name (default: the template's)

task.description: spawn: what the worker (or the taskforce's chair) should do; resume: optional, a new task for it

cwd.description: spawn: the worker's directory, relative to yours or absolute (default: yours); needs can_set_cwd; must be inside the team root or a git worktree of its repository; with template: the taskforce's directory, relative to yours or absolute, inside your root, a git worktree of its repo, or an allowed root (default: yours)

target.description: stop/resume/tail: the worker's name; admit: the solo session's name
